# Add a family member

## 1. Resolve the family Client

A family member is another investor profile within the account, not another authorized login. Read personal_client_id from the authorized account to identify the authenticated person’s linked family, when present. For machine keys or missing context, have the caller deliberately select an existing authorized Client; do not infer a personal family from a self investor, name or list order. Request investors:write for profile creation.

Do not assume the first Client in a list is the family, or that primary_investor always identifies it. Choose the intended existing Client explicitly before submitting the request.

## 2. Create the profile

Send the person’s name, relationship to the owner and the family Client ID. This stores a profile, not a user invitation or delegated authorization.

## 3. Associate their portfolio

Use member.id in the portfolio creation request. Render lists grouped by portfolio.investor. Names can repeat, so use IDs for all selection and update operations.

docs.title: Build fund autocomplete
docs.content:
# Build fund autocomplete

## Find a scheme without private account access

This example uses SDK 0.6.0 or later. Install the SDK and create an API key before you begin.

Use bharosa.markets.schemes.search({ query, limit }) with any active API key. No investor token, account ID or private portfolio permission is required. The HTTP operation is GET /v1/market-data/schemes/search. Existing mutualFunds.search remains account-scoped and still requires portfolios:read; it is not the baseline discovery method.

query is required: 2–100 characters, with at least two after trimming. limit is optional, from 1 to 20, and defaults to 10. Dates, pagination cursors, repeated parameters and unknown parameters are rejected. Send browser search input through your server; keep the API key private.

The response has object: list, data (an array), has_more (boolean), url (the route) and market_data with mode and notice. An empty data array means no matches; a failed request does not. If has_more is true, ask the user to refine the query rather than request a made-up cursor.

Each result has instrument metadata, scheme_id, plan_label, option_label and identity_status. Use scheme_id for NAV and expense lookups; instrument.id identifies the investment instrument; use it when creating a portfolio position. amfi_code and isin are present but nullable. Only resolved identities should be offered for a saved investment; preserve an unfamiliar response status rather than guessing its meaning.

latest_nav is present but nullable. When available, amount is an INR decimal string and date is the actual observation date. freshness includes status, checked_at, as_of, time_zone, nullable age_days and recent_within_days. Do not describe an older price as today’s price or substitute zero for null. data_mode and source identify the data context; label fixture results as fictional.

401 means the key is absent, expired or revoked; 429 means wait before retrying within the shared market quota. Preserve error codes and request IDs, keep the entered search text and do not replace a failed request with an empty list. Searching grants no portfolio access or analytics permission.

## Search as the user types

A person invests in a particular scheme, plan and option, not just a fund name. For example, Direct and Regular plans or Growth and distribution options must remain distinguishable in your selector. The API returns an instrument identity for the exact choice.

Search after the user has entered at least two characters, with limit between 1 and 20. Debounce input and ignore responses for older queries so a slow response cannot replace the latest results. Send the request through your server to keep credentials out of the browser.

Search puts exact identifier and name matches ahead of name prefixes, whole-word matches and broader matches. Numeric terms remain distinct: a search for 50 should prefer that token over 500. Results still require the user to choose the intended plan and option; do not automatically select the first match.

When a query ends with an explicit catalogue plan and optional option, such as Regular Growth or Direct Growth, search uses those labels to distinguish matching rows while ranking the base fund name. Omitting an option does not choose Growth for you, and omitting a plan does not default to Direct. Keep meaningful words such as Growth in the fund name; always confirm the returned scheme, plan and option before selection.

Search also separates copied punctuation such as commas, parentheses and slashes into terms. You can paste a complete scheme label while retaining Direct or Regular and Growth or IDCW. This is not typo correction or abbreviation expansion: check spelling and use the full name when shorthand finds nothing. Short fragments may produce broader matches, so always confirm the exact plan and option.

A search failure is a failed read, not evidence that a portfolio save occurred. Keep the entered draft and any saved holdings, explain that search is temporarily unavailable, and offer Retry fund search. Do not replace a failed request with an empty-results message or choose a similar scheme automatically.

Show the scheme name, plan_label and option_label together. An empty data array means there are no matching results. Allow selection only when identity_status is resolved; a conflicting identity is not safe to use for a save.

## Persist identity, not a label

Use the selected instrument.id in portfolio positions and save it alongside the entered current value. scheme_id, AMFI code, ISIN and display labels describe the reference but are not substitutes for instrument.id in those requests.

The SDK also exposes a MutualFund calculation handle. Its owner ID identifies the fund that owns the underlying investment portfolio; it is neither the asset management company (AMC) nor the investible scheme ID. When starting from a discovered instrument, use fromInstrument rather than guessing or converting an owner ID.

When reopening an editor, resolve the saved instrument IDs with the exact references endpoint. The missing array reports IDs that could not be resolved. Keep the saved position and show the unavailable reference instead of replacing it with a similarly named scheme.

## Treat NAV as reference data

Show latest_nav only when non-null, including its date. Show unavailable or stale states explicitly. Reference refreshes must not change manual holdings, quantity, or totals.

docs.title: Correct or update holdings
docs.content:
# Correct or update holdings

## 1. Load the current snapshot

Open the editor by retrieving `current_snapshot`. Copy all its positions into the draft and retain `snapshot.id` as expected_snapshot. This revision tells the API which version the user started editing. Keep monetary amounts as decimal strings throughout the form and request.

## 2. Send the complete set

A replacement sends the complete desired position list, not just the changed rows. Omit an instrument to remove it, or send an empty list to clear the portfolio. The request accepts 0–100 distinct instruments. Use the same effective date to correct that date’s values, or a later India date to record new values.

Include expected_snapshot and one new idempotency key for this edit. On success, update the editor with the returned positions and `snapshot.id`. The old snapshot remains unchanged, while `current_snapshot` now selects the new revision.

## 3. Reconcile conflicts

If another save wins, keep the user’s draft and fetch the newest snapshot. Compare old, draft and current values before asking the user to resolve differences. Do not merely swap expected_snapshot and resend.

docs.title: Handle stale edits & retries
docs.content:
# Handle stale edits & retries

## When the response is lost

A timeout does not prove the write failed. Retry the identical request with the original idempotency key within the 24-hour retention window. This recovers the original successful response when one exists.

## When a newer edit exists

409 snapshot_conflict means expected_snapshot no longer matches. Fetch `current_snapshot`, preserve the draft, and reconcile changed funds and values.

After the user confirms the reconciled complete set, submit the current snapshot ID and a new idempotency key. Blindly retrying the old body can overwrite someone else’s intended correction.

## When the retry window has passed

Read current holdings and compare with the intended operation before sending anything again. Show an uncertain-outcome state if the result cannot be established. A fresh key starts a new operation.

docs.title: Understand NAV freshness
docs.content:
# Understand NAV freshness

## What recent means

latest_nav is nullable. When present it contains amount, currency INR and date. freshness.status recent means its date is at most three Asia/Kolkata calendar days old. It does not guarantee the latest published NAV or a refresh SLA.

freshness.checked_at is the UTC instant when the API evaluated freshness. as_of is the India date used for that evaluation; age_days is calendar-day age, and recent_within_days is 3. These are not vendor ingestion timestamps.

## Handle every state

recent: display the NAV and date. stale: retain its date and indicate age. missing: show unavailable rather than zero. invalid: withhold the value; invalid dates, nonpositive amounts or wrong currency are not usable NAV. fixture identifies illustrative reference data.

Exact resolution returns missing IDs separately. Preserve saved holdings when a reference is missing or the provider returns 503. Retry lookup separately; do not rewrite snapshot instruments.

## NAV does not revalue manual holdings

Entered `current_value` is independent of reference NAV. Refreshing a fund does not change snapshot totals, quantities or cost basis. This interface supplies dated references, not historical NAV series or calculated returns.

docs.title: TypeScript SDK
docs.content:
# TypeScript SDK

## Install the TypeScript SDK

The TypeScript SDK is published on npm as `bharosa@0.6.0`. Use Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. Installing the package does not provision an account or enable API access.

In a new backend project, install the pinned version below from npm. Install scripts are disabled. Pinning the version keeps your initial integration on the release documented here.

Run these commands in your application folder. You do not need the SDK source repository or its contributor scripts.

The import check prints `Bharosa export: function`. The final command runs a small fictional-data example and prints `Installed SDK synthetic smoke passed`. Neither command needs an account or changes data. Next, configure the SDK for your own account or for an app serving other users.

## Choose the client for your task

Initialize `Bharosa` with your API key. The same client exposes baseline market data through `markets`; private own-account operations use the optional permissions selected when creating the key. Own-account selection defaults to `me`, so no account ID is needed. Keep the key on your server.

For market data without investor records, use `bharosa.markets` with any active API key. Omit `asOf` for latest NAV; supply a first-of-month `asOf` for historical NAVs, expense ratios, fund portfolios and fund holdings. These calls need no account ID or investor token. Baseline market access does not grant private portfolio analytics, scheme performance or category statistics; the latter two require accounts:read. `BharosaMarket` remains compatible.

For another person’s private account, `Bharosa` uses `delegated_application` authentication: your application key plus a user access token issued after that person authorizes the app. Your server receives and stores that authorization; the token is not a value a beginner should invent or paste into setup. Self-service application registration is available; check sign-in readiness and create its backend credential before starting consent. See the application quickstart for the prerequisites and consent flow.

Keep one immutable client per delegated user grant. Do not switch the account or token on a shared client between requests: each client should retain the credentials and account belonging to that grant.

The request and response models keep the API’s snake_case field names. SDK request options use names such as startingAfter for the HTTP `starting_after` cursor and `idempotencyKey` for the Idempotency-Key header. Annotate an investor creation body with InvestorCreate when storing it in a variable so TypeScript preserves the allowed relationship choices.

Requests accept only documented enum values. Responses may add new category strings over time; preserve an unfamiliar value and show an appropriate fallback instead of interpreting it as a known category. Object and resource-type discriminators remain strict.

## Optional: connect to another environment

For a separately configured test environment, both `Bharosa` and `BharosaMarket` accept an explicit `baseUrl` override. Use the HTTPS origin supplied for that environment and credentials issued for it. A local HTTP override also requires `allowLocalhostHttp: true`; use that only for a local test server. Normal production setup needs neither option.

An empty, null or invalid override is an error; the SDK does not silently fall back to production. Omit `baseUrl` to use the production default.

## Resource methods

Begin with accounts.retrieve() to read the authorized account. Use clients.list() and investors.list() to find the group and person for a portfolio. Each resource also supports retrieve(id); investors additionally supports create(body, options) and update(id, body, options).

Use mutualFunds.search({ query, limit }) to help a user select an instrument, then mutualFunds.references({ instruments }) to resolve exact saved instrument IDs. To save a portfolio, call portfolios.create(body, options). List or retrieve portfolios for their metadata, and use snapshots.retrieveCurrent(id) for their current positions. snapshots.create(id, body, options) saves a complete replacement.

For a calculation without saving, portfolios.build({ valuationDate, positions }) creates an in-memory portfolio. fromPositions is an equivalent alias. The supplied positions and their entries are copied and frozen; changing your original array will not change the handle. Use portfolios.create when you intend to persist records.

Both saved and in-memory portfolios expose assetMix(), sectorMix() and issuerMix(). Saved portfolios also expose currentSnapshot() and use their current snapshot for these calculations. The optional { `asOf` } selects the underlying funds’ holdings date cutoff; it does not rewind the investor’s positions.

A MutualFund handle represents the fund that owns an underlying portfolio. Use mutualFunds.fromId(ownerId) only with that owner ID, or fromInstrument(instrumentId) when starting from an investible instrument. The fund.portfolio property is a calculation handle, not a downloaded list of holdings. Scheme IDs and AMC IDs are different identities and cannot be substituted for owner IDs.

These calculations support India INR mutual-fund portfolios. Asset mix uses signed net exposure, so negative values or percentages above 100 can be valid. Sector and issuer mixes normalize equity contributions only, rather than describing the whole portfolio. Inspect source dates, warnings and reported precision before displaying results. Nonempty underlying holdings with zero net value produce an error.

Calculations are read-only server calls and do not require an idempotency key. Mutations use { `idempotencyKey` } in request options. The SDK does not obtain new user consent or resolve concurrent-edit conflicts for you. Account operations require the appropriate own-account permissions or delegated user consent.

## Observed positions and declared history

Use holding history when you need to answer what an investor held on a date, rather than only showing the latest manual snapshot. A holding belongs to a portfolio, an investment account or folio, and an asset. Two folios holding the same asset remain separate holdings; closed holdings remain available for historical queries.

After retrieving a saved portfolio, use holdings.list() to discover its holding IDs and holdings.retrieve(id) to obtain a handle. history.retrieve() returns the recorded observations, opening quantities, transactions and declarations. history.import(body, options) adds supported history, while history.canReconstruct(date) checks whether the portfolio has the required support for that date.

An observation is evidence for one particular date. holding.positionOn(date) returns an exact observation when present, even if its quantity is null because only a value was recorded. A later opening balance does not hide an earlier exact observation. An observation on one date is never silently carried backward to fill a missing date.

For other dates, reconstruction needs an opening quantity, buy/sell transactions, and a declared complete range. The opening is the quantity at the start of its date. Daily close includes that day’s transactions in their explicit sequence order. The investment account owns the timezone, which defaults to Asia/Kolkata. An opening balance is not recorded as an invented purchase.

A complete range is a statement by the source or user that the necessary history was supplied. It retains provenance and is not independent certification. Reconciling quantities alone does not create completeness. position_backing tells you whether evidence comes from snapshots, a transaction ledger, or both; it is separate from the completeness claim.

For dated portfolio calculations, call portfolio.on(`positionDate`), then assetMix(), sectorMix() or issuerMix(). The position date selects the investor’s holdings. valuationDate selects the date used to value them, and `asOf` selects the underlying funds’ holdings cutoff. Pass { valuationDate, `asOf` } to the mix method when those dates differ. Valuation defaults to `positionDate` and needs an existing provider NAV for that exact date; there is no stale-price or currency-conversion fallback.

Strict portfolio reconstruction needs a declared portfolio range and support for every stored holding, including closed holdings. history_unavailable and history_incomplete explain missing history support. External historical market dates must be month starts even with an account key; investor transaction and position dates remain unrestricted. historical_valuation_unavailable means the exact NAV needed for valuation is unavailable. An in-memory value-only portfolio cannot reconstruct earlier dates, and a fund calculation handle does not support investor dated views.

Imports require portfolios:write and an idempotency key. Within a source, transaction external_id identifies an event: replay applies it once and a conflicting payload fails. A later import may extend the same declared range forward, but cannot move its start or shrink it. Importing transactions alone preserves the existing declaration’s provenance.

New quantities use decimal strings with at most 20 whole digits and four fractional places; excess precision is rejected rather than rounded. Previously stored historical evidence retains its exact precision (up to 18 fractional places) in reads and calculations. A display rounded to four places is an approximation, not replacement evidence. Valuation fails explicitly if the result cannot be represented with the supported precision. An import is limited to 100 holdings and 5,000 transactions per holding. Transfers, splits, reversals, corrections, tax lots, performance calculations and public price imports are not supported. The published bharosa@0.6.0 SDK includes holding-history methods. Installing it does not establish hosted endpoint availability or grant access; confirm your service environment before using real account data.

## A small history example

Suppose a statement records 10 units at the start of 1 January 2026 and a buy of 3 units on 3 January. If the source declares the range 1–31 January complete, the supported daily-close position on 10 January is 13 units. The import example uses those fictional values; replace its portfolio, investment account and instrument IDs with your own records.

Import that history once with an idempotency key, retrieve it to confirm the stored source and range, then check history.canReconstruct("2026-01-10"). Use holding.positionOn("2026-01-10") for one holding. Without a complete range, those transactions do not establish that no other activity occurred: reconstruction is unavailable except where an exact observed position supplies point evidence.

For a portfolio mix, imagine asking for positions on 10 January, valuing them using 12 January NAVs, and selecting underlying fund holdings no later than 31 December. Use portfolio.on("2026-01-10") with { valuationDate: "2026-01-12", asOf: "2025-12-31" } on the mix method. These are three separate questions. All required investor history, exact valuation-date NAVs and eligible fund holdings must exist; otherwise the calculation returns an explicit error.

## HTTP stays explicit

Pass signal for cancellation, timeoutMs for the total request budget and maxRetries for bounded retries. Defaults are 30 seconds and zero retries. Retried mutations require a caller-supplied `idempotencyKey`; cancellation does not imply rollback. The SDK never follows redirects with credentials or caches account responses.

The published package supports named ESM and CommonJS imports under the browser export condition. This is module compatibility, not permission to put account keys in browser code. Browser applications still need an authorized server integration and their own trusted session transport; the private Bharosa adapter is not distributed here.

The SDK is MIT licensed, copyright Bharosa Technoserve Private Limited. This applies only to SDK material; the API and analytics implementation remain closed source. The SDK source is available at https://github.com/bhafin/sdk. Version 0.6.0 is published at https://www.npmjs.com/package/bharosa/v/0.6.0. Publishing the SDK does not activate the API or grant account access.

Use Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. ESM and CommonJS expose the same named `Bharosa` export and types. Install `bharosa@0.6.0`, then choose the account setup that matches your application.

HTTP requests use https://api.bharosa.finance. Sign in and manage credentials at https://app.bharosa.finance. The SDK selects the API origin automatically; a custom baseUrl is only needed for a separate test environment.
